subject.title: Exec/tool failures show "(see attached image)" and suppress model response

question: Should read-only exec-like tool failures with no delivered user reply emit a compact warning/fallback, or should OpenClaw keep suppressing those failures and rely on the broader placeholder cluster for follow-up?
rationale: Current docs say a tool-error fallback should be emitted when no renderable payload remains, but current code still has an explicit exec-like suppression branch for non-mutating exec/bash calls; changing that is a user-visible channel-noise contract choice.

options.title: Emit no-reply exec fallback
options.body: Change the warning/fallback policy so read-only exec-like failures remain quiet after a real assistant reply but emit a compact error when no user-facing reply was delivered.

options.title: Keep current suppression
options.body: Leave read-only exec-like failures quiet by default and require the model or channel layer to provide any user-facing explanation.

options.title: Split to canonical cluster
options.body: Close this issue after linking the placeholder part to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96857 and open a narrower owner-approved issue for the no-reply exec policy.

recommendation.title: Emit no-reply exec fallback
recommendation.body: Change the warning/fallback policy so read-only exec-like failures remain quiet after a real assistant reply but emit a compact error when no user-facing reply was delivered.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent merged history on the structured terminal-classifier side and is the best routing candidate for the terminal-state contract choice.
